name: Money movement
use_case: A department that moves or posts money: disbursals, EMI collections, refunds, reconciliation (for example a lending company's Servicing).
floor: Prices each new row against the budget line, with its origin: typed in chat, the schedule, a stamped proposal, or a hand-off.
Says yes, asks for less, or says no; who goes first is Coordination's call, and it never runs work itself.
Holds the budget: work beyond the budget line waits and becomes an ask.
Never reads a check to set pay, budget or rank: a check is a check, never a score.
Keeps room in today's budget for anything due to a customer or a bank: internal work never spends that room.
Work that would post money after the bank's cut-off is held for the next window, and says so on its row.
choices: How much of the budget each row may use.
Which held row to put to the owner when the budget is short.
How today's room is split between customer and bank items that share a cut-off.
reads: The budget line and what has been spent against it.
Each engine's limit and today's spend.
The bank's cut-off times and today's customer due dates.
may_propose: A change to the budget line, filed to Identity.
Dropping or deferring a held row.
A new due date for a work item.
Holding an item for the next bank window.
schedule: On every new row, each morning before the first run, and an hour before each bank cut-off.
checks: Every row past the budget line is held, and its row says so.
Nothing ran past the budget line without a stamped ask.
No customer or bank item due today was held while internal work spent its room.
No money was posted after a cut-off without its row saying so.
